Operating characteristics of the signal detection models by simulation

Source: R/sim_oc.R
sim_oc.Rd

Simulates blinded trials with sim_blinded, applies the selected models at each analysis, and summarizes the probability of declaring a signal (power, or the false positive rate when the study drug and placebo have the same distribution) and the posterior mean of the difference in cumulative incidence.

Usage

sim_oc(
  n_sim,
  design,
  models = c("BDRIBS1", "BDRIBS2", "EXP_BERN", "LL_BERN"),
  priors,
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  t_star = NULL,
  control = list(),
  seed = NULL,
  keep = FALSE
)

Arguments

n_sim

Number of simulated trials.

design

List of arguments of sim_blinded.

models

Character vector of models to apply.

priors

List of prior settings: bdribs (arguments lambda_hp, pt_hp and optionally df and p_prior of bdribs_post, used by "BDRIBS1" and "BDRIBS2"), expbern (the same arguments for expbern_post; bdribs is used when it is not given) and llbern (arguments mu_hp, sigma_hp, pt_hp and optionally df_p, mu_d_prior and sigma_d_prior of llbern_post).

rr0

Critical value of the relative risk.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

t_star

Time at which the relative risk of "LL_BERN" and the cumulative incidences are evaluated. Required for "LL_BERN".

control

List with elements EXP_BERN and LL_BERN, the control arguments of expbern_post and llbern_post. By default the convergence check is turned off.

seed

Optional seed passed to set.seed.

keep

Logical; if TRUE, the results of each simulated trial are returned.

Value

A list with elements

summary

Data frame with one row per analysis and model and the columns look, analysis_time, model, n_ok (successful fits), n_failed, prob_signal (proportion of trials with a signal), se (its Monte Carlo standard error), mean_prob (mean posterior probability), mean_ip_difference (mean of the posterior means of the difference in cumulative incidence at t_star), mean_observed_difference (mean of the difference between the proportions of subjects with the event in the study drug and placebo groups at the analysis, computed from the true group assignment), mean_n and mean_events.

truth

True cumulative incidences at t_star for placebo and study drug and their difference.

results

Data frame of the results of each trial (only when keep = TRUE).

Details

The models are "BDRIBS1" (bdribs_post with the total exposure time), "BDRIBS2" (bdribs_post with the total time at risk), "EXP_BERN" (expbern_post) and "LL_BERN" (llbern_post). The posterior functions are called with details = FALSE. A fit that fails is recorded as NA and counted in n_failed, and a warning with the first error message is given.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

sim_blinded

Examples

design <- list(n = 100, k = 1, accrual = 0, follow_up = 52,
               dist = "exponential", par_p = -log(0.9) / 52,
               par_d = -log(0.75) / 52)
oc <- sim_oc(n_sim = 20, design = design, models = c("BDRIBS1", "BDRIBS2"),
             priors = list(bdribs = list(lambda_hp = -log(0.9) / 52,
                                         pt_hp = 2000)),
             t_star = 52, seed = 1)
oc$summary
#>   look analysis_time   model n_ok n_failed prob_signal         se mean_prob
#> 1    1            52 BDRIBS1   20        0         0.0 0.00000000 0.6903407
#> 2    1            52 BDRIBS2   20        0         0.1 0.06708204 0.7447935
#>   mean_ip_difference mean_observed_difference mean_n mean_events
#> 1         0.06858147                    0.157    100       17.75
#> 2         0.09781049                    0.157    100       17.75
